record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Does every k-automatic word have an l-abelian complexity function that is itself k-automatic?

evidence.quote: (due to A. Parreau, M. Rigo, E. Rowland and E. Van- domme [64]): Any k-automatic word admits a ℓ-abelian complexity func- tion which is k-automatic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let k ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 1 be integers, and let A be a finite alphabet. An infinite word x = x_0 x_1 x_2 … ∈ A^ω is called k-automatic if there is a deterministic finite automaton with output that, on input the base-k representation of n, outputs x_n; equivalently, the k-kernel {(x_{k^i n + j})_{n ≥ 0} : i ≥ 0, 0 ≤ j < k^i} is finite.

For two finite words u, v over A and an integer ℓ ≥ 1, write u ∼_ℓ v if u and v have the same length and, for every word w ∈ A^* with |w| ≤ ℓ, the number of occurrences of w as a (scattered or contiguous, fixed convention: contiguous factor) factor of u equals the number of such occurrences in v. The relation ∼_ℓ is an equivalence relation on words of a given length, called ℓ-abelian equivalence (so ∼_1 is ordinary abelian equivalence).

For an infinite word x, the ℓ-abelian complexity function ρ^{(ℓ)}_x : ℕ → ℕ is defined by
   ρ^{(ℓ)}_x(n) = #{ [u]_{∼_ℓ} : u is a factor of x of length n }.

A function f : ℕ → ℕ (taking finitely many values) is called k-automatic if the sequence (f(n))_{n ≥ 0} is a k-automatic sequence in the above sense.

Question: Is it true that for every integer k ≥ 2, every integer ℓ ≥ 1, and every k-automatic infinite word x over a finite alphabet, the ℓ-abelian complexity function ρ^{(ℓ)}_x is itself k-automatic?
artifact.status_search_result: The related (and standard) conjecture is that the ℓ-abelian complexity of any k-automatic word is k-regular (the appropriate notion since the values can be unbounded). Parreau, Rigo, Rowland and Vandomme established this for the 2-abelian complexity of specific 2-automatic words such as the Thue–Morse and period-doubling words, and subsequent work (e.g., on Parikh-collinear fixed points and on generalized Cantor sequences) has extended automatic/regular abelian complexity results to further families. The general statement for all k-automatic words and all ℓ remains an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: A new approach to the ℓ-abelian complexity of 2-automatic sequences
status_evidence.snippet: They prove that the 2-abelian complexity sequences of the period-doubling word and the Thue–Morse word are 2-regular, contributing to the conjecture that the ℓ-abelian complexity of any b-automatic sequence is b-regular.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture is verified in special cases; general case open.

status_evidence.title: Automatic Abelian Complexities of Parikh-Collinear Fixed Points
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work establishes automaticity/regularity of abelian-type complexities for Parikh-collinear morphic fixed points, extending partial results toward the general conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial progress; full conjecture not yet proved.

status_evidence.title: On the 2-abelian complexity of generalized Cantor sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Studies 2-abelian complexity of specific automatic families, providing more partial evidence toward the regularity conjecture.
